points.description: Sets up the key transformation: inversion at D with power DB·DC composed with reflection in line AD (equivalently the map X→X' on ray/line through D with DX·DX'=DB·DC, taking points to the opposite side when on BC, same side when on AD). States/proves the pairs (A,H), (B,C), (E,F) correspond (e.g. DA·DH=DB·DC from cyclic BCEF / similar triangles). Any equivalent correct formulation (coordinates with D origin, etc.) is fine.

levels.says: Defines the map but verifies only some of the pairs, or does not justify DA·DH=DB·DC.

points.description: Identifies the image of G and of S: with Z the reflection of R over AD, shows R,Z are symmetric about AD and that G↔Z and S↔M correspond (e.g. via circle AHG mapping to itself / power of D, and harmonic or similar-triangle argument for S on EF and AH with M midpoint of AH).

levels.says: Notes R and Z are symmetric about AD only.
Establishes one of G↔Z or S↔M correctly with justification, not both.

points.description: Uses the map on line RS and the foot N: image of line RS is a circle through D, Z, M whose diameter from D ends at N'=image of N; hence N' is determined (DN·DN'=DB·DC) and O (midpoint of DN) is related to N'.

levels.says: States the image of RS is a circle through D, Z, M but does not connect N to the diameter endpoint.

points.description: Handles K, L and circle DKL (constructs the needed auxiliary point, e.g. T on line AT, or identifies images of K, L): shows circle DKL maps to a line (through images of K, L) and determines the image of P as a specific point, concluding that P and O are inverse points (images of each other) w.r.t. the map.

levels.says: Introduces a correct auxiliary point/construction (e.g. T) or images of K, L without completing the link to P.
Shows circle DKL maps to a line but the identification of P' with O is incomplete or unjustified.

points.description: Concludes DO·DP = DB·DC with O, P on the same ray from D (same side of D), i.e. O and P are corresponding points of the inversion of radius √(DB·DC).

Finishes: power of D with respect to circle OCP gives DC·DQ = DO·DP = DB·DC with Q on the same side of D as C, so DQ=DB with Q the reflection of B in AD's foot D; since AD ⊥ BC at D, AD is the perpendicular bisector of BQ, so AB=AQ. (Q=C-side point at distance DB from D.)

rubric.notes: Full marks need a valid proof; any correct alternative method (coordinates, other inversion description) earns the same marks. Part marks follow the listed observations (inverse pairs, R/Z symmetry, auxiliary point T, O/P inverse relation). The key claim is that O and P are inverse w.r.t. D with power DB·DC on the same ray; asserting it without justification earns at most P5 and P6.
rubric.answer_key: Coordinates: D=(0,0), B=(-b,0), C=(c,0), A=(0,a), H=(0,bc/a). Let Φ be inversion at D with power bc composed with reflection in AD (so Φ(B)=C, Φ(A)=H, Φ(E)=F). Since DA·DH=DB·DC, A↔H. Let Z be the reflection of R in AD; R,Z symmetric about AD, and Φ(G)=Z, Φ(S)=M (S=AH∩EF, M midpoint of AH; (S,M) are inverse as the pair (A,H) is harmonic with (S,M)). Line RS maps to circle through D, Z, M; N (foot from D to RS) maps to the antipode N' of D on this circle. Circle DKL maps to a line (via the images of K, L, using the auxiliary point T on line AT); this gives that P is the image of O, i.e. O, P lie on the same ray from D with DO·DP=DB·DC=bc. Then the circle OCP meets BC at C and Q; power of D: DC·DQ=DO·DP=bc with Q on C's side, so DQ=b=DB, Q=(b,0). Since AD⊥BC and DB=DQ, AB=AQ (A on the perpendicular bisector of BQ). QED.
